$comment: A fleet is ten jobs with ten models. `roleModels.<lane>.chain` is the ordered list of models that can serve that lane, best first, and the first rung the profile's `maxRetention` ceiling allows is the one that runs it. A chain is therefore ordered WITHIN this profile's ceiling, not globally: this profile's ceiling is may-train, so every rung is allowed and the chain starts with the model built for the job. The router walks the same chain when a route is spent. No model name in a lane is a promise that it will still exist next month, which is why every lane has a chain.
title: Ten jobs, every free model, one of them may train
notes: Every lane gets the model built for it: beam plans, Nemotron 3 Ultra reviews, Lightning sweeps, MiMo sees, GLM audits, Super VL reasons with the effort turned off. Five of the ten providers state that collected data may be used to improve the model, or log the session, so the profile as a whole is may-train and the generated config says so in its header. Install it for public or throwaway repositories.

utility.why: Cheapest route measured for a short auxiliary call: 49 reasoning tokens and 7.2s for a title, against 110 and 13.4s on big-pickle and 332 and 10.6s on nemotron-3.5-super-vl. It is also in every chain of this fleet, so a failover cannot leave the utility route pointing at a model that is not in the fleet.
